newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 26 to 833 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 26 to 833 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 833 as of Friday, up 26 from the prior week and 138 above the year-ago total of 695, Baker Hughes Inc. said.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by 21 to 701, while rigs working offshore rose four to 111. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose one to 21.
Among individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Oklahoma, which was up 10; Wyoming, which was up four and North Dakota, which was down two.
A total of 350 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up 17 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas was up nine at 481, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at two.
In Canada, the number of working rigs was down six at 408 vs. 382 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 168 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Friday, up five from the period ended Jan. 31.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 184, was 91.3 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area were unchanged at 105 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 106, a utilization rate of 99.1 percent.
The worldwide rig count rose four to 567 out of a total fleet of 606, making the utilization rate 93.6 percent.
